newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: RUGBY UNION-ENGLAND SCORE ANOTHER RECORD WIN.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-ENGLAND SCORE ANOTHER RECORD WIN.

text.p: England remained on course for a fourth Grand Slam in seven years with a record 46-6 victory over Ireland in the Five Nations championship at Lansdowne Road on Saturday.

England, who beat Scotland by a record 41-13 two weeks ago, pulled away in the final quarter with two tries each from wingers Jon Sleightholme and Tony Underwoood and one apiece for scrum-half Andy Gomarsall and flanker Richard Hill.
The remainder of England's scores came from the boot of outside-half Paul Grayson who kicked four penalties and landed two conversions.
Ireland's only points came from two penalties from outside-half Eric Elwood inside the opening 17 minutes.
